The first-stage mirror load is the likely culprit. M3 (diode load) is drawn at L=1.042 µm, but its mirror partner M4 is at L=0.15 µm, the minimum length, with the same W. M4 therefore sits in weak inversion (Vgs 0.503 V < Vth 0.687 V) with gm/gds of only 8.6. That makes the first-stage output conductance large and drops the DC gain. The matched mirror should use the same long L on both devices, so M4 is the odd one out.

M3 is second because it is the mismatched partner, and its Vth (1.022 V) is anomalous. M1 is third: it is off, but that follows from the input common-mode/offset condition, and its gain sensitivity is small (-0.038 dB), so it is less likely to be the injected fault.
